description: Policy controlling when a new analysis run raises a fresh alert versus updating an existing open alert.
rationale: A batch analysis run scores the same accounts repeatedly. Without deduplication, a nightly run would raise the same alert every night and bury the triage queue.
Deduplication must not hide genuinely new information, so a material escalation breaks out of the existing alert rather than updating it silently.

parts.name: typology_group
parts.source: sorted distinct rule metadata.typology of triggered rules
parts.notes: Grouping by typology rather than by individual rule code means adding a new rule to an existing typology does not re-alert every account.

notes: The key is stored in the unique Alert.dedup_key column, so the database itself prevents a duplicate open alert under a race.
Blank parts are rendered as '-' so positional meaning is preserved.
A rolling 7-day window means a persistent typology produces at most one alert per week per account.
dedup_window_start and dedup_window_end are recorded on the alert so an analyst can see exactly what period it covers.
Triage state is preserved: an analyst who acknowledged an alert must not have it reset to NEW by the next run.
first_seen_at is preserved so the queue can show how long a pattern has persisted.

break_out_conditions.description: Conditions under which a NEW alert is raised even though a matching open alert exists, because the situation materially changed.

conditions.name: band_escalation
conditions.test: new risk_band is higher than the existing alert's band
conditions.rationale: An account moving from HIGH to CRITICAL is new information that deserves its own queue entry.

conditions.name: score_jump
conditions.test: new score exceeds existing score by >= 15 points
conditions.rationale: A large jump signals a change in behaviour rather than the same pattern continuing.

conditions.name: new_typology
conditions.test: a triggered typology is absent from the existing alert's typology group
conditions.rationale: A second independent typology is corroborating evidence and must be visible.

conditions.name: new_complaint_linkage
conditions.test: a complaint correlation now exists that did not when the alert was raised
conditions.rationale: External corroboration is the single most actionable change and must never be buried in an update.

notes: If a closed alert's dedup key recurs within 14 days, a new alert is raised and linked to the closed one rather than reopening it, so the original disposition and its audit trail stay intact.
Beyond 14 days the recurrence is treated as an independent event.
Suppression is OFF by default and deliberately so: silently dropping alerts is a detection failure that is invisible in the queue.
When the per-account cap is reached, the run records a suppressed_count on the analysis run and emits an audit event instead of discarding the finding quietly.
Suppression must never apply to alerts carrying an escalate_to_human effect.
max_alerts_per_run bounds a runaway run; exceeding it marks the run PARTIAL rather than failing it outright.
